answer: Identity generation cost slows a Sybil flood to a glacier's pace: before an agent can trade, it must run a costly verifiable computation — a small kernel of useful work, such as solving a fresh benchmark puzzle — and publish the proof. The cost is trivial for one honest agent at the dawn of its first day, but spawning a thousand clones means paying the compute bill a thousand times, and the puzzle changes each epoch so pre-computed identities are worthless. Cheap copies melt away; only agents willing to pay the generation price enter the market.
